newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China's first half diesel imports soar.
newsitem.headline: China's first half diesel imports soar.

text.p: China's diesel imports soared in the first half of 1997 as buyers raced to replenish stocks, Chinese industry sources said on Monday.
However, the big jump in imports brought levels back into line with historical trends, they said.

Customs figures showed China imported 4.2 million tonnes of diesel in the first half of 1997, a 93 percent jump from the same period a year ago and almost matching 1996's total imports of 4.6 million tonnes.
"The year-on-year rise is very big, but don't forget the 1996 imports slumped from 1995. The comparison base is very low," said a trader with a Chinese state importer in Beijing.
Diesel imports in 1996 were more than 23 percent lower than the six million tonnes imported in 1995, which in turn were 0.8 percent lower than 1994 imports.
"Imports are just coming back to levels before last year and actually they should have risen more in the face of increasing demand at home," the trader said from Beijing.
Domestic stocks slumped late in 1996 as buyers turned away from imports in the face of international prices hitting a five-year high.
The low stocks sparked a wave of imports in 1997.
But imports in the second half were likely to slow down after the first half buying and bring annual imports back on track with levels seen before 1996.
"Unless the state issues fresh diesel import licences, imports in the second half can not be as big as in the first half," the source said from Beijing, noting high diesel stocks.
China has not issued fresh import licences for the third quarter. Some traders said the state might not issue licences for the rest of the year because domestic stocks piles were ample.
Increasingly, mechanised agriculture as well as electric power generation, particularly in southern China, are expected to hike China's use of diesel.
State oil company officials have forcast China's diesel demand at 55.7-56.7 million tonnes in the year 2000 and 83.4-88.6 million tonnes in 2010.
China's combined production and imports in 1996 totalled 47.85 million tonnes.
China does not encourage diesel imports and boosted domestic output to meet rising demand.
Output in 1996 climbed 11.20 percent to 43.2539 million tonnes from 1995.
"Refineries have been asked by the state to produce more diesel instead of imports," a source with China National Chemicals Imports and Exports Corp (SINOCHEM) said.
The rise continued in the first half of 1997, with China's diesel output jumping 12 percent from a year ago to 23.75 million tonnes, the state data showed.
